1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes — adjust downward for the first 5–7 days.
2. Model underestimates prices during mean-reversion phases — increase forecast slightly when recent values are significantly above historical average.
3. Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below the peak observed in the 7-day window prior.
4. Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to true price drops — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days when true outcome shows downward momentum.
5. Model overfits to recent high volatility — reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term noise; use 30-day rolling average as a smoothing anchor.
6. Model underestimates true price volatility in low-price regimes — increase forecast variance slightly when price is below 70% of 30-day moving average.
7. Model fails to capture seasonal or policy-driven price shifts — add a 1–2 day buffer for policy-related price corrections (e.g., auction adjustments, cap changes).
